title: A factorization modulo I of a monic polynomial into coprime monic factors lifts after an etale extension trivial modulo I
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal and $f\in A[x]$ a monic polynomial, with image $\bar f\in(A/I)[x]$. Let $\bar f=\bar g\bar h$ in $(A/I)[x]$ with $\bar g,\bar h$ monic and generating the unit ideal of $(A/I)[x]$. Then there exist a ring map $A\to A'$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and the induced map $\alpha:A/I\to A'/IA'$ is an isomorphism, and monic polynomials $g',h'\in A'[x]$ with $f=g'h'$ in $A'[x]$ ($f$ mapped to $A'[x]$) whose images in $(A'/IA')[x]$ are $\alpha(\bar g)$ and $\alpha(\bar h)$ ($\alpha$ applied coefficientwise).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0ALH (lemma-lift-factorization-monic) and its proof (uses Algebra Example Tag 00UA algebra-example-factor-polynomials-etale, Lemma Tag 07M0 lemma-localize-upstairs, Algebra lemma-map-between-etale and lemma-surjective-flat-finitely-presented)

proof.text: *Degrees and the universal ring (Stacks: 'Say $\deg\bar g=n$, $\deg\bar h=m$ ... consider $R\to S$ of Algebra, Example 00UA ... set $B=A\otimes_RS$').* Choose integers $m,k\ge0$: if $A/I\neq0$, $m=\deg\bar g$ and $k=\deg\bar h$; then $\bar f=\bar g\bar h$ is monic of degree $m+k$ (product of monic polynomials over a nonzero ring), and since $f$ is monic and $A/I\ne0$, $\deg f=\deg\bar f=m+k$. If $A/I=0$, take $m=\deg f$, $k=0$. Put $n=m+k=\deg f$. In both cases $f$ is monic of degree exactly $n$, and $\bar g,\bar h$ are monic of degree exactly $m,k$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-universal-coprime-factorization-ring] (over the zero ring that condition is empty). Let $B$, $G,H\in B[x]$ be the $A$-algebra and polynomials of [lem-weil-pbc-universal-coprime-factorization-ring] for $(A,m,k,f)$: $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale, $f=GH$ in $B[x]$, and $A$-algebra maps $B\to C$ correspond to coprime factorizations of $f$ over $C$ by $\varphi\mapsto(\varphi(G),\varphi(H))$. (Stacks uses $B=A\otimes_RS$ and later a localization $B_g$ chosen by More on Algebra 07M0 near $V(J)$; here $B$ is already the localization $(A\otimes_RS)[1/\operatorname{Res}(G,H)]$, etale over $A$ everywhere by Algebra Example 00UA, so 07M0 is not needed: the resultant maps to a unit of $A/I$ in step 2 because $\bar g,\bar h$ are coprime, which is what 07M0's $g$ provides.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0ALH (lemma-lift-factorization-monic)

proof.text: *The point $B\to A/I$ (Stacks: 'The $A$-algebra map $B\to A/I$, $1\otimes b_i\mapsto\bar\beta_i$, $1\otimes c_i\mapsto\bar\gamma_i$ maps $g_B,h_B$ to $\bar g,\bar h$. The displayed map is surjective').* $A/I$ is an $A$-algebra, $\bar g,\bar h\in(A/I)[x]$ are monic of degree exactly $m,k$ (step 1), $\bar g\bar h=\bar f$ and $\bar g,\bar h$ generate the unit ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-universal-coprime-factorization-ring] (3) with $C=A/I$ there is a unique $A$-algebra map $\varphi:B\to A/I$ with $\varphi(G)=\bar g$ and $\varphi(H)=\bar h$. It is surjective, since already its restriction along $A\to B$ is the quotient map $A\to A/I$. As $\varphi$ is $A$-linear, $\varphi(IB)=I\cdot(A/I)=0$, so $\varphi$ induces a homomorphism of $A/I$-algebras $s:\bar B:=B/IB\to A/I$ with $s(\bar y)=\varphi(y)$ for $y\in B$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0ALH (lemma-lift-factorization-monic)

proof.text: *$\bar B$ is etale over $A/I$ and $s$ splits off an idempotent (Stacks: 'Since $A/I\to B_g/IB_g$ is etale, also $B_g/IB_g\to A/I$ is etale (Algebra 00U7). Hence there exists an idempotent $e\in B_g/IB_g$ such that $A/I=(B_g/IB_g)_e$ (Algebra 00U8)').* Since $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale (step 1), $\operatorname{Spec}\bar B\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-quotient-base-change]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-idempotent-splitting] to $R=A/I$, $S=\bar B$ and the $A/I$-algebra map $s$ of step 2 (that node contains the steps 00U7 and 00U8 of Stacks): there is an idempotent $\bar e\in\bar B$ with $s(\bar e)=1$, $\ker s=(1-\bar e)\bar B$, and $s$ induces an isomorphism of $A/I$-algebras $\sigma:\bar B_{\bar e}\xrightarrow{\sim}A/I$, $\bar y/\bar e^r\mapsto s(\bar y)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0ALH (lemma-lift-factorization-monic)

proof.text: *The ring $A'$ and its etaleness (Stacks: 'Choose a lift $h\in B_g$ of $e$. Then $A\to A'=(B_g)_h$ ...').* Choose $b\in B$ whose image in $\bar B=B/IB$ is $\bar e$ (the quotient map is surjective), and put $A'=B_b$ (localization at $\{1,b,b^2,\dots\}$), an $A$-algebra via $A\to B\to B_b$. $\operatorname{Spec}B_b\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is an open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1); $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale (step 1); and $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is their composite (functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$), hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0ALH (lemma-lift-factorization-monic)

proof.text: *$A/I\to A'/IA'$ is an isomorphism (Stacks: implicit in 'is a solution to the problem').* The ideal $IA'$ is the extension to $B_b$ of $J=IB\subseteq B$ (both are generated by the images of the elements of $I$). By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute] (with $B$, $J=IB$, $b$) the map $\bar B\to A'/IA'$ induced by $B\to B_b$ makes $A'/IA'$ the localization of $\bar B$ at the powers of $\bar e$; so there is an isomorphism $\lambda:\bar B_{\bar e}\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/IA'$, $\bar y/\bar e^r\mapsto[y/b^r]$. Put $\psi=\sigma\circ\lambda^{-1}:A'/IA'\xrightarrow{\sim}A/I$ (step 3), an isomorphism with $\psi([y/b^r])=\varphi(y)$ for $y\in B$ (as $s(\bar e)=1$). Let $\alpha:A/I\to A'/IA'$ be the map induced by $A\to A'$, i.e. $\alpha(\bar a)=[a\cdot1]$. For $a\in A$, $\psi(\alpha(\bar a))=\varphi(a\cdot1_B)=\bar a$ since $\varphi$ is an $A$-algebra map. So $\psi\circ\alpha=\mathrm{id}_{A/I}$, and since $\psi$ is bijective, $\alpha=\psi^{-1}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0ALH (lemma-lift-factorization-monic)

proof.text: *The factorization (Stacks: 'with factorization given by the image of the factorization $f_B=g_Bh_B$ in $A'$').* Let $\iota:B\to A'=B_b$ be the localization map, an $A$-algebra map, and put $g'=\iota(G)$, $h'=\iota(H)$ (coefficientwise). Since $G,H$ are monic of degree exactly $m,k$, so are $g',h'$; in particular $g',h'$ are monic (in the zero ring every polynomial is monic). Applying $\iota$ to $f=GH$ gives $f=g'h'$ in $A'[x]$ ($\iota$ restricted to $A$ is the structure map). Reduction modulo $IA'$: let $\pi:A'\to A'/IA'$ be the quotient map. Then $\psi\circ\pi\circ\iota=\varphi$ on $B$ (step 5: $\psi([y/1])=\varphi(y)$). Hence, coefficientwise, $\psi(\pi(g'))=\varphi(G)=\bar g$ and $\psi(\pi(h'))=\varphi(H)=\bar h$ (step 2), so $\pi(g')=\psi^{-1}(\bar g)=\alpha(\bar g)$ and $\pi(h')=\alpha(\bar h)$. Together with steps 4 and 5 this proves the lemma. (In Lean: the images of $g'$ mod $IA'$ are the first component of homEquiv applied to $\pi\circ\iota$, and homEquiv_comp_fst/snd with $\psi$ give the comparison, as recorded on [lem-weil-pbc-universal-coprime-factorization-ring].)

lean.statement: theorem exists_etale_lift_monic_coprime_factorization {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (f : A[X]) (hf : f.Monic) (g₀ h₀ : (A ⧸ I)[X]) (hg₀ : g₀.Monic) (hh₀ : h₀.Monic) (hfactor : f.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = g₀ * h₀) (hcoprime : IsCoprime g₀ h₀) : ∃ (A' : Type u) (_ : CommRing A') (φ : A →+* A'), let J : Ideal A' := I.map φ let α : A ⧸ I →+* A' ⧸ J := Ideal.quotientMap J φ Ideal.le_comap_map AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)) ∧ Function.Bijective α ∧ ∃ g' h' : A'[X], g'.Monic ∧ h'.Monic ∧ f.map φ = g' * h' ∧ g'.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J) = g₀.map α ∧ h'.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J) = h₀.map α
